name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Tuesday 28 August 1990 (English cryptic)

clue.text: Partly waxed till the end of March?

blocks.note: first meaning: the moon's phase when it has waxed to a half disc
second meaning: January to March, the opening three months of the year

explanation.walkthrough: 'Waxed' suggests polish or hair removal, but it is the moon growing; the question mark admits the second meaning is a calendar period, not a phase.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon's first quarter is the phase when it has grown to half-lit, and a year's first quarter runs from January to March.

clue.text: Vagrant late for treatment by mistake

indicators.note: treatment given by mistake is handling gone wrong, so the letters come out in a muddled order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tramp turns up too late for medical care because of an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' belongs to the letters as well as to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A floater is a person who drifts from place to place or job to job without settling.

clue.text: Hire again, free

blocks.note: first meaning: to lease out once more
second meaning: to set loose or liberate

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'free' look like part of a rental deal; it is a separate meaning of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-lease is to let a property out again, while release as a verb means to let something go.

clue.text: Siren indicating temperature at lock

blocks.note: TEMP is the everyday short form of temperature
placed next to
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A warning siren showing the temperature at a canal lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siren' and 'lock' suggest an alarm and a canal; the siren is a seductive woman, the lock is hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Sirens lured sailors with song, so a siren is a seductive woman, a temptress.

clue.text: Mothers' Union's back to front attire casts a shadow

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer, which is a noun

indicators.note: back to front means the word is turned round so its end comes first

blocks.note: MU is the abbreviation for the Mothers' Union, a Church of England women's charity
a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: A churchwoman's clothes put on back to front leave a shadow over her.
explanation.walkthrough: UM, then BRA. The definition is loose: the answer is the shadow itself, cast by an eclipsing body.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, especially that thrown by the moon or earth in an eclipse.

clue.text: Hot and inflamed at pole? Must be changed on map!

blocks.note: red-hot: red describes heat
inflamed skin is raw
N, north, is one of the earth's poles

explanation.surface: Heat and redness at the North Pole mean the map needs revising.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary or map that has been redrawn has been changed by drawing it again.

clue.text: English trees? Nonsense!

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
two trees: a yew and an ash

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claim about English trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is a dismissive word for talk meant to deceive, a synonym of nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: A second drink, and we'll see how they live

blocks.note: first meaning: pub talk for another round, the next half-pint
second meaning: from the saying about seeing how the rest of society lives

explanation.walkthrough: 'The other half' is a jokey offer of a second drink; the saying 'how the other half lives' means the rich or poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Offering 'the other half' is buying a further drink, and the other half are the people whose lives differ from ours.

clue.text: Rough cowl on chimney

blocks.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
LUM is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney

explanation.surface: A rough cowl, the cap fitted over a chimney pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' reads as an adjective for the cowl, but it is a noun: a rough is a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, as a noun, is a violent lout or thug, which is what a hoodlum is.

clue.text: Put to death about 500 with a pillow and a board?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the execution word is wrapped around the number

blocks.note: to behead is to execute by cutting off the head
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An execution, oddly followed by a pillow and a board, as if describing a scaffold.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by description: the pillow and the headboard are what you find at that end of a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The head end of a bed, where the pillow lies against the headboard, is described by those two items.

clue.text: Implicated with no difference, as between 26 and 1 across or 7, possibly

definitions.text: as between 26 and 1 across or 7, possibly

indicators.note: a difference is a change, so these letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone implicated in a crime, found to have made no difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no difference' looks like a phrase, but 'no' is fodder and 'difference' signals the shuffle. The definition points to whole numbers and fractions like a first quarter or the other half.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2.25 or 1.5 the decimal point is the dot dividing the whole numbers from the quarter or half after it.

clue.text: Striking actors are evicted

blocks.note: workers on strike are said to be out
the actors in a production are its cast

explanation.surface: Actors on strike find themselves thrown out of their lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcast used as an adjective describes someone driven out or expelled, which is what evicted people are.

clue.text: Old language of a sheep with the reverse of intelligence

indicators.note: the reverse of something reads it the other way round, back to front

blocks.note: taken as written
a ram is a male sheep
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue spoken by a sheep that is the opposite of clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic language of the Near East, spoken in Jesus's time.

clue.text: Mass of the fifth order

indicators.note: read here as taking away the letter standing fifth in the following word

blocks.note: the closing letter of this word
the word with its fifth letter, an R, dropped

explanation.surface: A dense gathering of the fifth rank in some hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: This parse is tentative: the answer is sure from its definition and crossings, but the setter's exact route to the H is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a great crowd or multitude, and a mass of people is the same thing.

clue.text: Swearing at meat in Howards' place

blocks.note: effing is a mild swearing word, from the letter F
ham is cured meat from a pig

explanation.surface: Someone cursing over dinner at the home of the Howard family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Howard family, Earls of Effingham, take a title from this Surrey village; Lord Howard of Effingham commanded against the Armada.
explanation.definitionFit: Effingham in Surrey is the seat in the noble title held by a branch of the Howard family.

clue.text: No seats left in old train going fast?

blocks.note: a vehicle with no seats left is full
old trains ran on steam

explanation.surface: A packed old train racing along with standing room only.
explanation.definitionFit: Full steam, as in 'full steam ahead', means at top speed, the pressure of a steam engine at maximum.

clue.text: Catches in genuine practice

indicators.note: in says the first word is placed inside the second word

blocks.note: something genuine is real
to catch a remark is to hear it

explanation.surface: Something caught in the act during a real practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches' looks like the definition, as in catching fish, but it means hearing a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a performance before the real thing.

clue.text: Port which is built round a river

indicators.note: something built is assembled, so these letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A harbour town constructed around a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built round' suggests a container, but the letters are simply assembled anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Harwich is a ferry port on the Essex coast of eastern England.

clue.text: Stimulation of fissiparous alkaloids

indicators.note: of here means made from part of the words that follow, which hold the answer within them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A chemical note on alkaloids that split apart and act as stimulants.
explanation.walkthrough: Fissiparous means tending to split, which neatly suits a word broken across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is the state of being excited or stimulated, so it means stimulation.

clue.text: I fled in disorder from Cuba

definitions.note: a description of a person rather than a synonym

indicators.note: in disorder means jumbled up, so the letters are mixed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone escaping chaos on the island of Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a man from Cuba: Fidel Castro, its leader in 1990. The surface suggests a refugee fleeing him.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Cuba from 1959, so his first name identifies the famous man from Cuba.

clue.text: Anticipate payment - poet's gold's included

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a fee is a payment
ore is a poetic word for gold, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Expecting payment because a poet's gold has been counted in.
explanation.walkthrough: Poets use 'ore' for gold, as in Milton's 'new-spangled ore'.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee something is to expect it before it happens, which is to anticipate it.

clue.text: Lady losing point due for game

indicators.note: losing a point means a compass point, a single letter, is dropped

blocks.note: the word without its E, east being a compass point
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A woman who drops a point she was owed in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a noblewoman, wife of a duke, and a titled lady.

clue.text: Bearing left from landing-place

blocks.note: an air is a manner or bearing
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A compass bearing taken leaving from a jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a compass direction, but it is demeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport is where aircraft come down, so it is literally a place for landing.

clue.text: Saw work for 9 coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: a nonet is a musical piece for nine players

explanation.surface: Seeing a composition for nine performers about to be staged.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' is the number nine, not a reference to 9 across. 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a fine-toothed carpenter's saw, here shortened to its first word.

clue.text: Address your company, command er properly or you'll get a blow

blocks.note: the form of address for an officer
OC, officer commanding, is the title of a company's commander
CO is the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Parade-ground advice: speak properly to your commanding officer or you will be struck.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan splits 'commander' in two. 'Blow' looks like a punch, but it is a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot wind blowing from North Africa, and a blow is a strong wind.

clue.text: Boy who is loving and giving makes one shudder

blocks.note: the nursery rhyme says Friday's child is loving and giving; FRI'S is Friday's shortened
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A generous, affectionate lad who somehow gives people the creeps.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face' gives each weekday's child a trait; Friday's is loving and giving. So Friday's son: FRI'S SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden thrill or shiver of emotion, a single shudder.

clue.text: Electroplated stone rendered by sculptor

blocks.note: EP is the abbreviation for electroplated, as in EPNS
stein is German for stone: the word rendered into German

explanation.surface: A plated stone carving made by a sculptor.
explanation.walkthrough: EPNS, electroplated nickel silver, is stamped on cutlery. 'Rendered' looks like carving, but it means translated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a famous modernist sculptor working in Britain.

clue.text: Integers in general anaesthetics?

blocks.note: general, as in a general anaesthetic, means affecting the whole body
anaesthetics are numb-ers: things that numb

explanation.surface: Integers turning up in a list of general anaesthetics.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of 'numbers' as things that numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers are the counting numbers with no fractional part, also called whole numbers.
